prompt: Search for the top 3 LLM orchestration frameworks in 2025 (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, or others). For each framework, find and summarize: (1) core architecture and design philosophy, (2) pricing model, (3) community adoption metrics (GitHub stars, npm/pip downloads if available). Present a structured comparison table. Cite your sources with URLs.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Facts and claims match the cited sources and are factually correct

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All three frameworks covered with all requested dimensions (architecture, pricing, adoption)

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Sources are real, accessible URLs from authoritative sites (official docs, GitHub, reputable tech publications)

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Output is a coherent comparative analysis, not just dumped search snippets. Includes a comparison table.

prompt: Research the most recent critical security vulnerabilities (CVEs) affecting the Go programming language standard library disclosed in 2024 or 2025. For each CVE found, provide: the CVE ID, affected Go versions, severity rating (CVSS score if available), a brief description of the vulnerability, and the recommended mitigation or patched version. Cite official sources (Go blog, NVD, GitHub advisories).

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: CVE IDs, versions, and severity ratings are correct and verifiable

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: Covers multiple recent CVEs, not just one. Includes all requested fields for each.

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites official Go security advisories, NVD, or GitHub security advisories

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Organized clearly with actionable mitigation guidance, not raw data dumps

prompt: Research the current market landscape for local-first AI inference engines that run LLMs on consumer hardware (e.g., llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, vLLM, etc.). Identify at least 4 key players. For each, research: (1) supported model formats, (2) hardware requirements, (3) performance benchmarks if available, (4) business model / licensing. Conclude with an analysis of which approach wins for cost arbitrage (running inference locally vs cloud APIs). Cite all sources.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Technical details (model formats, hardware requirements, performance numbers) are correct

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: At least 4 tools covered with all 4 requested dimensions. Cost arbitrage analysis included.

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Sources are real URLs from official docs, benchmarks, or reputable tech publications

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Includes a comparative analysis with a clear conclusion on cost arbitrage, not just a feature list

prompt: Research how the GGUF model format works for running LLMs locally. Cover: (1) the evolution from GGML to GGUF and why the change was made, (2) the internal structure of a GGUF file (header, metadata, tensor data), (3) available quantization levels (Q2_K through Q8_0) and their quality/speed/size tradeoffs, (4) which quantization levels are recommended for different use cases (chat, code generation, embedding). Browse the llama.cpp documentation or GitHub repo for authoritative details. Cite sources.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Technical details about GGUF format, quantization levels, and tradeoffs are correct

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All 4 requested topics covered in depth. Quantization comparison table included.

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: Cites llama.cpp repo, GGUF spec docs, or authoritative technical posts

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Provides actionable recommendations, not just technical specs. Clear narrative arc from history to practical guidance.

prompt: Research the state of durable execution engines in 2024-2025. Cover at least: Temporal, Restate, and Inngest. For each, research: (1) core architectural pattern (event sourcing, deterministic replay, or other), (2) language SDK support, (3) deployment model (self-hosted, cloud, both), (4) production adoption (notable companies using it), (5) developer experience strengths and weaknesses. Synthesize a comparative analysis that would help a CTO decide between them for a new microservices project. Must browse at least 3 different source URLs for depth. Cite all sources with URLs.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Architectural patterns, SDK support, and deployment models are factually correct

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: All 3+ engines covered with all 5 requested dimensions. Comparative analysis present.

criteria.name: Source Quality
criteria.description: At least 3 distinct source URLs cited. Sources are official docs, case studies, or reputable tech publications.

criteria.name: Synthesis
criteria.description: Provides a CTO-level decision framework, not just a feature matrix. Weighs tradeoffs and makes a recommendation.
